current_example.problem: Suppose $\mathbf a=[7,\, 2,\, 4]^T$ and $\mathbf b=[2,\, 3,\, 1]^T.$ Find the Euclidean distance $d_2$ between $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that the Euclidean distance is defined as

$$
d_2(\mathbf a,\mathbf b) =\|\mathbf a-\mathbf b\|_2
$$

where for an $N$-dimensional vector $\mathbf v,$

$$
\|\mathbf v\|_2 = \sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^N |v_i|^2}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{d}_{2}(a,b) & =‖a-b{‖}_{2} \\  & ={‖[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]‖}_{2} \\  & =\sqrt{|7-2{|}^{2}+|2-3{|}^{2}+|4-1{|}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{35} \\  & ≈5.916,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
